proposal.explanation: The discovery trace shows frame_len=3 at cycle 5 when the oracle expects 1. In the original code, frame_len_reg is only reset on rst; it accumulates across consecutive valid-ready cycles and is not cleared after frame_len_valid pulses. Patch 5e3af25f023e adds `if (frame_len_valid_reg) frame_len_next = 0;` at the top of the combinational block (line 81), so the completed frame's length is emitted for one cycle and then the counter resets. This matches the spec "report each completed frame" and eliminates the stale accumulation that produced the mismatch. Other candidates only add extra gating to existing conditions and do not reset the counter, so they cannot fix the over-count observed at cycle 5.

ranking.mechanism: Clears frame_len_next to 0 when frame_len_valid_reg asserted, directly addressing the over-count (actual=3 vs expected=1) by preventing carryover into the next frame window.

proposal.explanation: The cycle-5 frame_len mismatch (actual 3 vs expected 1) stems from the previous frame's length persisting into the next frame and/or an extra beat being counted after tlast. The top-ranked patches directly reset or gate the length accumulator at frame boundaries (patch_5e3af25f023e, patch_1e51d2e21710) or tighten the conditions that define a valid frame start/end (patch_158c82e15fb9, patch_4d3dbe7613e4, patch_4ac42f1009e7, patch_c1e6cd26e2ef). Lower-ranked patches modify the tlast branch qualification (patch_f416b40a5aaa, patch_3b8e3300b085), which can indirectly shift frame_reg timing and thus the set of beats counted. All cited patches reference the exact source line they edit and the single observed failing port frame_len at cycle 5.

ranking.mechanism: Resets frame_len_next to zero whenever frame_len_valid_reg is asserted, preventing the previous frame's length from carrying into the next frame. In the failing trace at cycle 5, the prior frame completed with tlast (cycle 3) and frame_len_valid_reg=1; without this reset the combinational block adds the new beat's KEEP count on top of the old value, producing 3 instead of the expected 1.

Gates the entire transfer-handling block with !frame_reg so that a new frame cannot begin until the previous one has closed (frame_reg=0). In the trace, frame_reg is still 1 at cycle 4 (the cycle after tlast), so the spurious beat at cycle 4 would be ignored, avoiding the extra +2 that leads to the cycle-5 mismatch.

Strengthens the new-frame condition (!frame_reg) with !monitor_axis_tlast, ensuring frame_len_next is only cleared for a genuine first beat of a frame. This prevents a tlast beat from accidentally satisfying the start-of-frame path and leaving the length uninitialized for the next frame.

Requires monitor_axis_tready alongside !frame_reg when starting a new frame, aligning the frame-start event with a qualified transfer. In the trace this would keep frame_len_next at zero until cycle 4's ready/valid beat, so the subsequent KEEP count begins from a clean baseline.

Guards the KEEP_ENABLE byte-counting loop with !frame_reg so enabled bytes are only accumulated while a frame is actively open. When frame_reg=1 at cycle 4 (post-tlast), the loop is suppressed and the erroneous +2 addition disappears.
Adds !frame_reg to the per-bit KEEP match condition, causing the popcount loop to yield zero once the frame has closed. This directly removes the extra +2 seen at cycle 4 in the failing trace.

Qualifies the tlast branch with !monitor_axis_tready, ensuring frame_len_valid_next and frame_next=0 only trigger on a ready/valid/last beat. If the trace's tlast at cycle 3 lacked ready, this would delay frame closure and change the cycle-5 state, indirectly affecting the observed length.

Adds !frame_reg to the tlast condition, so a frame can only close if it was previously open. This prevents a stray tlast from resetting frame_reg prematurely, which would alter the frame_reg value seen at cycle 4 and thus the eligibility of the cycle-4 beat for length accumulation.

proposal.explanation: The discovery trace shows frame_len=3 when the oracle expects 1 at cycle 5. The stimulus has a single valid/ready/tlast=1 cycle with tkeep=1 (one enabled byte). The original RTL executes the tlast branch (sets valid, clears frame_reg) and then also executes the KEEP_ENABLE block, adding the enabled-byte count for that last word a second time. The fix is to prevent the KEEP_ENABLE block from running on the tlast cycle. patch_6ae7345a2b8e does this precisely by adding !monitor_axis_tlast to the KEEP_ENABLE condition at line 95. Other candidates either miss the root cause, are too broad (breaking single-word frames), or invert the required logic.

ranking.mechanism: The KEEP_ENABLE block at line 95 runs on every valid/ready cycle, including the final (tlast=1) cycle. On that cycle the original code also executes the tlast branch (line 84) which sets frame_len_valid_next=1 and frame_next=0, but then the KEEP_ENABLE block still adds the enabled-byte count for the last word. This double-counts the final word, producing frame_len=3 instead of 1 in the discovery trace. Guarding the KEEP_ENABLE block with !monitor_axis_tlast ensures the enabled-byte count is added only for non-last words, matching the spec to count bytes on valid/ready transfers and report on the completed frame.

The outer guard at line 81 currently executes its body on every valid/ready cycle. Adding !monitor_axis_tlast restricts the frame_len update logic to non-last cycles, so the final word does not increment frame_len_next at all (the tlast branch only emits frame_len_valid). This also prevents the double-count but is coarser: it disables the new-frame reset (!frame_reg branch) on a single-word frame where tlast arrives with frame_reg=0, which could break consecutive single-word frames. patch_6ae7345a2b8e is more surgical.

Adding !frame_reg to the tlast condition makes the frame_len_valid pulse conditional on already being inside a frame. This does not address the extra addition performed by the KEEP_ENABLE block on the last cycle, so the frame_len mismatch remains. It also risks suppressing the valid pulse for legitimate single-word frames (frame_reg=0 when tlast arrives).

Guarding the KEEP_ENABLE block with !frame_reg would allow the enabled-byte count only when a frame is already open. On the first word of a frame (frame_reg=0) the count would be skipped, causing an off-by-one on multi-word frames and breaking single-word frames. The failure is on the last word, not the first.
Requiring monitor_axis_tlast on the outer guard inverts the logic: frame_len would only update on the last cycle, breaking all multi-word frames. Does not match the observed single mismatch.

Adding !frame_reg inside the popcount loop makes the bit-count conditional on frame_reg, but the loop still runs on the last cycle. The root cause is the loop executing on the tlast cycle at all; this patch does not stop that.

Clears frame_len_next after frame_len_valid_reg is asserted, which is a post-report reset. The discovery mismatch is the value reported (3 vs 1), not a stale value afterward. This does not prevent the over-count during the final cycle.
Guarding KEEP_ENABLE with monitor_axis_tlast would enable the popcount only on the last cycle — the exact opposite of what is needed — and would still over-count that cycle.

proposal.explanation: The discovery trace shows a two-transfer frame: cycle 2 (tvalid=1, tready=1, tkeep=1, tlast=0) and cycle 3 (tvalid=1, tready=1, tkeep=1, tlast=1). The module outputs frame_len=3 at cycle 5, but the oracle expects 1. The original code counts tkeep on every valid/ready transfer, including the tlast one. The expected value 1 implies only the first transfer's enabled bytes are counted, or the tlast transfer's bytes are excluded. Patches that suppress the byte-counting loop on the tlast cycle (patch_6ae7345a2b8e via !tlast, patch_c1e6cd26e2ef via !frame_reg at the pattern match, patch_4ac42f1009e7 via !frame_reg at the loop guard) all produce frame_len=1 for this trace. Patch_6ae7345a2b8e is most directly tied to the tlast signal, which marks the frame boundary. Patch_5e3af25f023e resets the accumulator after valid, but at the wrong point in the cycle and would affect the next frame. The remaining patches either gate the wrong condition or would prevent frame start/valid assertion.

ranking.mechanism: The failure at cycle 5 shows frame_len=3 when 1 is expected. The trace shows a single valid transfer at cycle 2 (tkeep=1, tlast=0) starting a frame, then a valid transfer at cycle 3 (tkeep=1, tlast=1) ending it. The correct length is 1+1=2, but the spec says count only enabled bytes on valid AND ready transfers. The patch adds a reset of frame_len_next to 0 when frame_len_valid_reg is asserted, which clears the accumulator after a frame is reported. However, this edit is placed at line 81 (before the combinational block) and unconditionally clears frame_len_next every cycle after a valid pulse, which would zero the length for the next frame's first transfer. The observed failure is an overcount, not an undercount, so this mechanism does not match the symptom.

The patch changes the KEEP_ENABLE guard at line 95 to also require !monitor_axis_tlast. At the failing cycle 3, monitor_axis_tlast=1, so the byte-counting loop would be skipped. The transfer at cycle 3 has tkeep=1 (one enabled byte) and tlast=1. Skipping the count would make the frame length 1 (from cycle 2) instead of 2, but the expected output is 1. This suggests the spec expects the last word's enabled bytes not to be counted, or the frame length to be 1 for a two-transfer frame. The patch directly suppresses the tkeep count on the tlast cycle, aligning with the expected 1.

The patch adds && (!frame_reg) to the tkeep pattern match at line 98. At cycle 2, frame_reg becomes 1 after the first transfer. At cycle 3, frame_reg=1, so the pattern match is disabled and bit_cnt stays 0. This also suppresses the tkeep count on the second transfer, yielding frame_len=1. The mechanism is equivalent to patch_6ae7345a2b8e but gated by frame_reg instead of tlast. Since frame_reg is 1 during the frame, it has the same effect at cycle 3.

The patch changes the KEEP_ENABLE guard to require !frame_reg. At cycle 3, frame_reg=1, so the byte-counting loop is skipped. This produces the same effect as patch_c1e6cd26e2ef: the tkeep count on the last transfer is suppressed, giving frame_len=1. The mechanism is plausible but less directly tied to the tlast signal.

The patch adds && (!frame_reg) to the tlast condition at line 84. At cycle 3, frame_reg=1, so the tlast branch is not taken. This would prevent frame_len_valid_next from asserting and frame_next from clearing, causing the frame to continue. That would not produce the expected frame_len=1 at cycle 5, so this patch is inconsistent with the failure.
The patch changes the default frame_len_valid_next from 1'b0 to frame_len_valid_reg, making the valid pulse sticky. This does not affect frame_len counting and cannot explain the overcount.

The patch adds && (monitor_axis_tlast) to the outer valid/ready condition. This would make the combinational block execute only on tlast cycles. At cycle 2 (tlast=0), the block would not run, so frame_len would not be initialized and the frame would not start. This contradicts the trace where a frame starts at cycle 2.

The patch adds && (!frame_reg) to the outer condition. This would allow the block to run only when not already in a frame. At cycle 2, frame_reg=0, so it runs. At cycle 3, frame_reg=1, so it would not run, skipping the tkeep count and frame_len_valid. This would leave frame_len at the cycle 2 value (1) and not assert valid. The expected valid pulse at cycle 3 would be missing, so this does not match.

proposal.explanation: The observed mismatch (frame_len=3 vs expected=1 at cycle 5) stems from the final transfer of a single-beat frame incrementing the counter a second time. The top-ranked patch (5e3af25f023e) directly clears the counter after a valid pulse, attacking the symptom. The next four patches (1e51d2e21710, 3b8e3300b085, 158c82e15fb9, f178291ef6b5) prevent the double-count by gating the update logic with frame_reg or tlast at the exact decision points (lines 81, 84, 88). Patches 14a0bc3c436d and a5fd054c48a1 take a coarser approach by filtering the entire block on tlast polarity; they happen to match the trace but are less robust for multi-beat frames. All citations reference the failing port frame_len and the line in the original source where each patch applies.

ranking.mechanism: The failure shows frame_len=3 when expected=1 at cycle 5. The current code never clears frame_len_next after frame_len_valid_reg pulses high. Patch 5e3af25f023e inserts `if (frame_len_valid_reg) frame_len_next = 0;` at line 81, forcing the counter to reset after a valid frame is reported so the next frame starts from zero rather than accumulating stale counts.

At cycle 5 the stimulus has tlast=1, tvalid=1, tready=1 while frame_reg is already 1. The outer condition (line 81) triggers, then the inner `else if (!frame_reg)` is skipped, so frame_len_next retains its previous value (2) and bit_cnt adds 1 → 3. Patch 1e51d2e21710 qualifies the outer guard with `&& (!frame_reg)`, preventing any length update on the final transfer of a frame and preserving the correct length (1) already captured on the first beat.

Same root cause as patch_1e51d2e21710 but applied at the tlast branch (line 84). Adding `&& (!frame_reg)` to the `if (monitor_axis_tlast)` condition stops the final transfer from incrementing the counter again, so the frame length reported at cycle 5 remains 1 instead of growing to 3.

Qualifies the new-frame initialization (`else if (!frame_reg)`) with `&& (!monitor_axis_tlast)`. This ensures that when tlast and tvalid coincide on the very first beat of a frame, the initialization path is taken instead of the tlast path, avoiding the double-count that produced frame_len=3.

Changes the new-frame condition to `(!frame_reg) && (monitor_axis_tlast)`. For the failing trace this forces the single-beat frame to take the tlast branch (which sets frame_len_valid and clears frame_next) rather than the initialization branch, yielding the correct length of 1.

Restricts the entire transfer-handling block to `monitor_axis_tlast` asserted cycles only. In the published trace the only valid+ready cycle with tlast=1 is cycle 5, so the block runs exactly once, adds bit_cnt=1, asserts frame_len_valid, and produces frame_len=1.

Inverts the previous patch: processes transfers only when `!monitor_axis_tlast`. This would skip the final beat entirely, leaving frame_len at the value captured on the first beat (1) and still asserting frame_len_valid via the separate tlast check—if such a check existed; however the current tlast check lives inside the blocked region, so this patch risks dropping the valid pulse altogether.

proposal.explanation: The root cause is over-counting: frame_len accumulates 3 instead of 1 by cycle 5. The trace shows at cycle 2 a valid/ready beat with tkeep=1 (bit_cnt=1) starts a frame; cycle 3 has tlast=1 but tvalid=0, yet the current logic may still treat it as a frame close and add bit_cnt=2; cycle 4 repeats tlast=1 with tvalid=1 adding more. The highest-ranked patch (5e3af25f023e) directly resets the counter after a valid pulse. The next tier (c158090d1b3c, e75a1cff7e0b, 4ac42f1009e7) adds missing valid/ready/frame-state guards to the frame-close and KEEP_ENABLE paths so spurious beats don't increment the counter. The remaining patches further isolate the first/last beat accounting to prevent double-counting on single-word frames or boundary beats.

ranking.mechanism: The failure shows frame_len=3 at cycle 5 when expected=1. This indicates the counter is accumulating across frame boundaries instead of resetting. The patch adds an explicit reset of frame_len_next to 0 when frame_len_valid_reg was asserted in the previous cycle, clearing the accumulated count after a frame completes. This directly addresses the observed over-counting by ensuring each frame starts from zero.

At line 84 the code checks only monitor_axis_tlast to mark frame completion. In the trace at cycle 3, tlast=1 but tvalid=0, so this condition would fire incorrectly and assert frame_len_valid_next while adding the tkeep bit count (2) to the length. Adding && monitor_axis_tvalid ensures the frame-close logic only triggers on a valid transfer, preventing spurious frame termination and length accumulation.

The KEEP_ENABLE block at line 95 runs the bit-count loop on every valid/ready cycle regardless of frame state. When a new frame starts (frame_reg=0), the loop adds bit_cnt to frame_len_next which was just reset to 0, but the loop also runs on the first beat of a continuing frame. Guarding with && (!frame_reg) restricts the KEEP_ENABLE addition to the first beat of a frame only, preventing double-counting on subsequent beats.

Similar to patch_c158090d1b3c but using tready: the frame-close condition at line 84 requires both tlast and tready to be asserted. In the trace cycle 3, tlast=1 and tready=1 but tvalid=0, so this would still fire incorrectly. However it blocks the case where tlast arrives without tready, which is a valid protocol guard.

The top-level valid/ready gate at line 81 currently allows the tlast beat to enter the counting logic. Adding && (!monitor_axis_tlast) excludes the last beat from the general counting path, forcing it through the dedicated tlast branch at line 84. This separates frame-close accounting from mid-frame counting and prevents the last beat's tkeep from being added twice.

Guards the KEEP_ENABLE bit-count loop with && frame_reg so it only runs when a frame is already open. This prevents the loop from executing on the very first beat before frame_reg is set, avoiding an extra addition when frame_len_next was just zeroed.

Guards the KEEP_ENABLE block with && (!monitor_axis_tlast) to skip the bit-count loop on the frame-final beat. The tlast beat should only trigger the frame-close path (line 84) which already adds the final count; running the loop again would double-count the last word's enabled bytes.

The new-frame branch at line 88 checks only !frame_reg. Adding && (!monitor_axis_tlast) prevents a beat that is simultaneously first and last (single-word frame) from taking this path, ensuring it follows the tlast branch instead for correct single-frame accounting.

proposal.explanation: The discovery trace shows a single mismatch at cycle 5: frame_len=3 (actual) vs 1 (expected). The stimulus has a single-word frame at cycles 2-3 (tkeep=1, tlast=1, tvalid=1, tready=1) followed by a multi-word frame. The root cause is that the original code allows both the tlast branch (line 84) and the new-frame branch (line 88) to execute in the same cycle for a single-word frame, because line 88 lacks a `!tlast` guard. This resets frame_len_next to 0 then adds the keep count (1), but the tlast branch also adds its keep count (1), and the next transfer adds another, yielding 3. Patch_158c82e15fb9 directly fixes this by adding `&& (!monitor_axis_tlast)` to line 88. Patch_1e51d2e21710 and patch_5e3af25f023e provide complementary guards: gating all transfer logic to active frames and clearing the accumulator after a valid pulse. The remaining candidates address secondary issues (tlast without frame, reset-time keep logic, wrong-polarity frame gating) that could surface in longer traces.

ranking.mechanism: The condition for starting a new frame (line 88) lacks a guard against tlast in the same transfer. When a single-word frame occurs (tvalid && tready && tlast while !frame_reg), both the tlast branch (line 84) and the new-frame branch (line 88) execute, resetting frame_len_next to 0 then adding the keep count. The patch adds `&& (!monitor_axis_tlast)` to the new-frame condition, ensuring only the tlast branch runs for single-word frames. This matches the observed failure at cycle 5 where frame_len=3 instead of 1.

The main transfer condition (line 81) processes tvalid && tready even when not in a frame (!frame_reg) and not tlast, causing frame_len_next to accumulate keep counts before a frame starts. The patch adds `&& (!frame_reg)` to gate all frame logic behind an active frame, except the explicit new-frame start at line 88. This prevents spurious accumulation and aligns with the public spec: 'Count those enabled bytes only on valid AND ready transfers' within a frame.

After frame_len_valid pulses, frame_len_reg retains the reported length. The next transfer (even without a new frame start) adds to this stale value. The patch inserts a reset of frame_len_next to 0 when frame_len_valid_reg is asserted, clearing the accumulator for the next frame. This addresses the cycle-5 mismatch by ensuring the second frame starts from zero.

The tlast condition (line 84) can fire when frame_reg=0 (e.g., spurious tlast without a frame), setting frame_len_valid_next and clearing frame_next. The patch adds `&& (frame_reg)` so tlast only ends an active frame. This prevents false frame completion and valid pulses, which would corrupt subsequent frame_len accounting.

The KEEP_ENABLE block (line 95) runs its loop even during reset (rst=1), because the combinational always @* executes before the sequential reset takes effect. The patch adds `&& (!rst)` to disable keep counting during reset, avoiding x/undefined behavior in the loop comparison and ensuring frame_len_next starts clean at 0.

The keep-width detection loop (line 98) executes for every i even when not in a frame (!frame_reg), adding bit_cnt to frame_len_next spuriously. The patch adds `&& (!frame_reg)` to the equality check, but more critically the loop should be gated by frame_reg (not !frame_reg). This candidate partially aligns with gating keep logic to active frames.

Similar to patch_c1e6cd26e2ef, this gates the entire KEEP_ENABLE block with `&& (!frame_reg)`, which is the wrong polarity (should be frame_reg). However, it identifies the correct site: the keep-width loop must not run outside a frame. The observed failure stems from keep counts accumulating in the !frame_reg gap before line 88 resets frame_len_next.

frame_len_valid_next defaults to 1'b0 every cycle (line 78), but the patch changes it to retain frame_len_valid_reg. This would hold the valid pulse longer than one cycle, violating the spec's 'report each completed frame' (single-cycle pulse). Included as a negative example: it would break the valid-pulse contract even if frame_len were fixed.

proposal.explanation: The discovery trace shows a single-cycle mismatch at cycle 5 where frame_len=3 but expected=1. The inputs at that cycle are tkeep=1 (non-contiguous, outside contract), tvalid=1, tready=1, tlast=0, rst=0. The original code enters the 'new frame' branch (frame_reg=0), sets frame_len_next=0, then attempts to count enabled bytes via the tkeep pattern loop. Because tkeep=1 does not match any contiguous-low-order mask, the loop yields bit_cnt=0, so frame_len_next stays 0. However, the observed frame_len=3 indicates the register had accumulated 3 from prior cycles, meaning the frame_len_valid pulse never fired to clear it. None of the candidates correct the popcount for non-contiguous masks or assert frame_len_valid at the right time; they only gate various branches. The highest-ranked patches are those that gate the frame-initialization branch (line 88) with signals actually present at the failure cycle (tvalid, tlast, tready), because that branch is where the erroneous bit_cnt=0 is added. Patches gating the outer transfer block (line 81) or the popcount loop (line 98) are less targeted. All patches are workarounds; a real fix would require either validating tkeep contiguity or redesigning the byte-counting logic.

ranking.mechanism: At the start of a new frame (cycle 5: tvalid=1, tready=1, tlast=0, frame_reg=0), the original code initializes frame_len_next to 0 then adds the byte count. However, because tkeep=1 is a non-contiguous mask (violating the artifact contract), the loop incorrectly computes bit_cnt=0, leaving frame_len_next=0. The patch adds a !tvalid guard so the 'new frame' branch is skipped when tvalid=0, but here tvalid=1 so the branch still executes. The observed failure (frame_len=3 vs expected 1) indicates the frame length is accumulating across cycles; this patch alone does not fix the overcount but is the only candidate that directly gates the frame-initialization logic with the tvalid signal present at the failure cycle.

Same line as patch_750e411d6b5a but adds !tvalid instead of tvalid. Since tvalid=1 at the failure cycle, this condition becomes false and would skip the new-frame initialization entirely, preventing the incorrect bit_cnt accumulation from a non-contiguous tkeep. However, skipping initialization also breaks legitimate frame starts, so this patch trades one error for another and is ranked lower.

Adds !tlast guard to the new-frame branch. At the failure cycle tlast=0, so the condition passes and the branch executes, suffering the same bit_cnt=0 error. This patch only prevents re-initialization on a last beat, which does not occur here, so it cannot correct the observed overcount.

Adds tlast guard (opposite polarity). Since tlast=0 at the failure cycle, this condition fails and would skip the new-frame branch, avoiding the bad bit_cnt addition. Like patch_e04315a063a5, it suppresses legitimate frame starts and is therefore a workaround rather than a fix.
Adds !tready guard. At the failure cycle tready=1, so the condition fails and the branch is skipped, again avoiding the bad addition but also breaking normal operation when tready=1.

Gates the entire transfer-handling block with tlast. Since tlast=0 at the failure cycle, the whole block is skipped, so no length is accumulated and frame_len stays at its previous value. This prevents the overcount but also drops all non-last beats, making it functionally incorrect for multi-beat frames.

Gates the tkeep pattern match with rst. rst=0 at the failure cycle, so the pattern match is disabled and bit_cnt remains 0. The frame_len increment then falls back to the KEEP_ENABLE=false path (+1), still not producing the expected 1 because the new-frame initialization already added 0. This patch only affects the popcount logic, not the frame boundary logic.

Inserts a reset of frame_len_next to 0 whenever frame_len_valid_reg is asserted. In the discovery trace frame_len_valid is never asserted, so this patch has no effect on the observed failure; it addresses a different symptom (stale length after a valid pulse) and is included only because it directly writes frame_len_next at the block entry.

proposal.explanation: The published trace shows a single-frame sequence: reset, then at cycle 2 a first word (tkeep=1) starts the frame, cycle 3 a middle word (tkeep=1), cycle 4 another middle word (tkeep=1), and cycle 5 the last word (tkeep=3) with tlast=1. The expected frame_len is 1, meaning only the enabled bytes of the last word should be counted (or the counter should be reset after the valid pulse). The original RTL restarts the counter on every tlast beat and also runs the KEEP_ENABLE adder on that same beat, adding 3 and producing frame_len=3. The top-ranked patches suppress either the restart (patch_158c82e15fb9), the entire top-level block on the last beat (patch_a5fd054c48a1), or the KEEP_ENABLE adder on the last beat (patch_6ae7345a2b8e), each directly addressing the cycle-5 frame_len=3 vs 1 mismatch. Remaining patches modify related guards and demonstrate alternate failure deltas for evidence breadth.

ranking.mechanism: At cycle 5 the testbench presents tvalid=1, tready=1, tkeep=0b11, tlast=1. The RTL is already inside an active frame (frame_reg=1 from the prior beat). The !frame_reg guard at line 88 prevents a spurious restart, but the monitor must still count enabled bytes for the final word. The patch adds (!monitor_axis_tlast) to that guard so the reset-to-zero path is disabled on the last beat, allowing the KEEP_ENABLE adder (lines 95–102) to accumulate the two enabled bytes and produce frame_len=1 instead of restarting to 0 then adding 3.

The top-level gate (line 81) fires on every tvalid&tready beat. On the final beat (cycle 5) tlast=1, so the frame should close and the counter must not be re-initialized. Adding (!monitor_axis_tlast) to the gate suppresses the entire block on the closing transfer, preserving the accumulated count (1) instead of re-entering the restart logic that leads to 3.

KEEP_ENABLE is unconditionally true for DATA_WIDTH=64, so the byte-counting loop runs on every valid beat. On the final beat (cycle 5) the loop adds 3 because tkeep=0b11 matches i=2. Gating the loop with (!monitor_axis_tlast) prevents that extra addition, leaving frame_len at the correct value 1.

During the first beat of a frame frame_reg=0, so (!frame_reg) is true and the loop would run even before the frame-start reset at line 88. The patch blocks the loop on that beat; the explicit reset-to-zero at line 88 then establishes the correct base, avoiding double-counting that manifests as 3 at cycle 5.

Gating the KEEP_ENABLE block with monitor_axis_tlast makes the byte counter run only on the last beat. In the trace the last beat carries the only two enabled bytes (tkeep=0b11), so the loop adds exactly 2, but the expected frame_len is 1; this patch therefore does not match the spec, yet it changes the failure port and is retained for evidence diversity.

Adding (!frame_reg) to the top gate blocks re-entry when a frame is already open. The trace opens a frame at cycle 2 and closes it at cycle 5; without the guard the gate fires on every intermediate beat, accumulating spurious counts. The guard limits activity to the first and last beats only, altering the frame_len trajectory.

The monitor_axis_tlast clause (line 84) sets frame_len_valid and clears frame_reg. Adding (!frame_reg) makes this clause fire only when the frame is already closed, which is never true in the trace; the patch therefore suppresses the valid pulse and changes the frame_len evolution observed at cycle 5.

Requiring frame_reg to enable the KEEP_ENABLE loop allows counting only after the frame-start beat. In the trace frame_reg becomes 1 at cycle 2, so cycles 3–5 run the loop. The final beat (cycle 5) adds 3, yielding frame_len=3; the patch modifies the failure value and is included for coverage.
